conventions.convention: The Lorentzian signature is (-,+,+,+); future nonzero causal vectors pair negatively with the time-orientation field N. Zero is not a causal vector.

Causal curves are continuous and locally absolutely continuous in charts, with nonzero future causal velocity almost everywhere. Reachability is reflexive separately; constant curves are excluded from this curve class. Inextendibility means absence of a point limit at the relevant parameter end.
A Cauchy set is met at exactly one parameter value by every two-sided inextendible causal curve, counting repeated visits to the same point separately.

Normal inverse domains are open and star-shaped. Strict convexity includes unique affinely parametrized joining segments for closure endpoints; distinct endpoints have segment interiors inside the open set, while equal endpoints give the constant segment.
P(p,q) is the terminal tangent at q of the radial geodesic from p; D²(p,q)=g_p(exp_p⁻¹(q),exp_p⁻¹(q)) is signed squared displacement, not a metric distance.
Lorentzian length of an absolutely continuous causal curve is the Lebesgue integral of sqrt(-g(γ′,γ′)); the derivative and integrand are interpreted almost everywhere.
The auxiliary complete metric is h′=(1+|df|²_h)h, where h=g+2n-flat⊗n-flat and f is a smooth nonnegative proper exhaustion. Riemannian distance and completeness are componentwise.
The finite density measure is a regular Borel measure of total mass one; its Borel domain is not silently identified with its completion.
The volume time is t=ln μ(I⁻(p))−ln μ(I⁺(p)); it is continuous, with no smoothness asserted. The subsequent smooth temporal function T is a separate construction.
The complete flow field is X=∇T/g(∇T,∇T), so X is future timelike and X(T)=1; completeness is asserted for this normalized field.

Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are explicit premises of the general absolutely continuous causal calculus and its consuming causal results; the density and auxiliary metric constructions distinguish their more limited choice uses.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, in a strictly convex normal set C, local causal and chronological reachability from p are the exponential images of the future causal-or-zero and future timelike cones. Causal curves have length at most sqrt(-D_p²(endpoint)); the stated null and equality cases force radial geodesic representations.

Every point p and open neighborhood O of p admit a coordinate ball C⊂O which is a normal neighborhood of each of its points, with a unique contained joining geodesic and the stated strict closure-endpoint convexity.

Assuming Countable Choice and Dependent Choice and a complete proper auxiliary Riemannian metric, arclength-parametrized causal curves with convergent initial points admit subsequences converging uniformly on compact parameter intervals to nonconstant causal limits; eventual half-line domains give future-inextendible limits, with the stated chart estimate.

Under Countable Choice, h=g+2n-flat⊗n-flat is positive definite and admits the proper-exhaustion conformal factor h′=(1+|df|²_h)h with |df|_h′≤1; each connected component is complete and its closed bounded subsets are compact. The additional absolutely continuous distance–length assertion assumes Dependent Choice.

For positive finite-length arclength-parametrized causal curves with convergent endpoints, bounded positive limiting lengths give joining causal limits after the specified common-domain reparametrization; zero limiting length gives coincident endpoints and a constant continuous limit; unbounded lengths give two inextendible tails with the stated sequential closure relation.
Assuming Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, existence of a Cauchy set implies absence of nonconstant closed causal curves, strong causality, and compactness of every causal diamond.

On the stated globally hyperbolic manifold with the normalized finite density measure, t(p)=ln μ(I⁻(p))−ln μ(I⁺(p)) is continuous, strictly increasing on distinct causally related points, diverges at the respective ends of every inextendible causal curve, and every real level is a Cauchy set.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated conically bounded product chart has a Cauchy neighborhood of its zero slice. Every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface without boundary admits the stated variable-width temporal collar whose intrinsic interior domain of dependence makes the entire hypersurface Cauchy and is globally hyperbolic.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, refined sums of local separations converge to Lorentzian length for the stated causal curve and every allowed mesh-zero partition sequence, independently of the selected normal balls; uniform convergence of causal curves on a common compact parameter interval gives limsup L_g(α_k)≤L_g(α).

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated globally hyperbolic manifold admits a smooth temporal function T with Cauchy hypersurface levels and divergent values along inextendible causal curves; X=∇T/g(∇T,∇T) is complete with X(T)=1, its flow gives the stated product diffeomorphism, and the metric has the stated orthogonal decomposition.

concerns.concern: Clause (a3) promises a constant C 'depending only on the chart and h' for every chart of the kind in dominating-cone clauses (a),(b). Step 5.2 assumes that h_ab are bounded on all of U, while Fact L6 first shrinks to a neighborhood compactly contained in a larger chart. The statement does not explicitly require that buffering or boundedness. On M=B_1⊂R⁴ with flat Lorentzian g and complete proper auxiliary metric h=(1−|x|²)⁻² times the Euclidean metric, the identity chart satisfies the adapted cone bounds, but vertical arclength curves near the boundary require unbounded constants in Δs≤CΔx⁰. The assertion needs an explicit chart scope, unless 'kind produced' is intended to include the proof's unstated precompact extension condition. The local causal-limit conclusion itself uses only buffered charts.

Fact L1 says a nonzero displacement is future causal exactly when 'v⁰≥|v_vec|>0'. This excludes v=(1,0,0,0), which is future timelike and hence future causal. The cited flat-cone supplier instead states v⁰≥|v_s| for nonzero v and separately concludes v⁰>0. The worked null legs remain valid, but the asserted prerequisite criterion is false.

The first Remark says 'global hyperbolicity is equivalent to closedness of the causal relation plus compactness of the truncated cones.' The stated theorem proves only the forward implication. The reverse assertion without a causality hypothesis is false: the flat Lorentzian four-torus with periodic time and spatial coordinates is totally vicious, so J⁺=J⁻=M and the causal relation is closed; every truncated cone is empty or the compact M, but closed timelike curves prevent global hyperbolicity.

Step 3.1 defines F(s,t)=D²(p(s),q(t)) but writes ∂_tF(s,0)=2g_q(P(p,q),w). At general s the position vector must be P(p(s),q). The displayed expression is correct at s=0, which is the only value needed for the conclusion.

The Example claims 'complete gradient flow', and the Summary calls X=∂₀/T′ its 'gradient field'; the comparison Remark likewise calls ∂₀ the gradient field of t. The actual gradients are ∇T=−T′∂₀ and ∇t=−∂₀. Completeness is proved for X=∇T/g(∇T,∇T). For the displayed rational T, the genuine ∇T reaches a slab boundary in finite flow time because the integral of 1/T′ over (0,1) is finite. The formulas and normalized-flow proof are sound, but the terminology asserts a materially different property if read literally.

The 'What is proved here' paragraph says 'complete gradient flow'. The cited splitting theorem asserts completeness of the normalized field X=∇T/g(∇T,∇T), not of ∇T itself. The same distinction needs to remain explicit in the page summaries.

The explicit-splitting paragraph gives T=t/(1−t)−1/t, whereas the assigned example defines T=t/(1−t)−1/t+1. This additive constant matters for the example's identification of Σ_1/2 with the zero level: the example has T(1/2)=0, while the page formula gives −1.

alerts.finding: Clause (e) defines H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)\I⁻(D⁺(S)) but describes it as points 'that are not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. Membership outside I⁻(D⁺(S)) instead means there is no point of D⁺(S) chronologically after the given point. The prose reverses the direction of the displayed formula.

Fact L5 cites thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic 'clause (b)' for compact causal diamonds. Its clause (b) is strong causality; compact diamonds are clause (c). Fact L1 similarly attributes global hyperbolicity to clauses (a),(b), omitting the compactness clause needed for that conclusion.

seams_checked.note: Causal curves, reflexive reachability, no-limit inextendibility, parameter-counted Cauchy sets, strong causality and global hyperbolicity are used at the supplied scope. General AC-calculus consumers carry Countable Choice and Dependent Choice.

Uses the smooth boundaryless four-manifold, (-,+,+,+) signature, smooth time orientation, metric-selected connection and musical maps. Mathematical deductions remain separate from the optional physical readings.

The finite-density construction takes the metric coefficient sqrt(|det g|), explicitly proves its absolute-Jacobian transformation law and does not import the supplier's orientation assumption for a volume form. No field equation is assumed.

Observer normalization, rest-space projection and positivity, observer pairing and adapted-chart existence retain their pointwise or local scope. The full adapted shear correctly preserves n=∂₀ while changing the time coordinate.

Uses local geodesic existence, smooth dependence, scaling, d exp at zero, parallel transport and Gauss lemma at their stated mathematical scope. Absolutely continuous causal length is defined locally rather than attributed to the piecewise-C¹ timelike proper-time definition.

The slab and flat-model uses otherwise match their suppliers, but ex-gr-null-legs-corner-push-up L1 incorrectly restates the future-causal criterion as v⁰≥|v_vec|>0, excluding purely temporal future timelike vectors. Recorded in concerns.

Flat geodesic and gradient computations use the metric-selected connection and musical maps. The complete-flow calculation explicitly concerns the normalized gradient field; misleading gradient terminology is recorded separately.
The examples use mathematical flat Lorentzian models, future orientation and inverse-metric gradients without an empirical or free-fall assertion.

Dust residual step 7.1 uses the componentwise complete proper auxiliary metric and the eventual-domain past half-line limit theorem without assuming strong causality of the open solution domain. Geometric and dust developments use intrinsic Cauchy neighborhoods, including the variable-width hypersurface clause, at the supplied scope.

The inspected uses preserve Cauchy side decomposition, local exponential inverses, push-up, compact-length limits, length upper semicontinuity and intrinsic restart neighborhoods. Quotient arguments explicitly apply local manifold results inside genuine second-countable members. The incorrect clause locator in lem-gr-compact-past-above-cauchy-set is routed as an alert; the required compactness proposition is supplied by clause (c).

The direct edge is the push-up use in ex-gr-flat-restart-level-set step 3.1: p≤γ(t₂)≪q implies p≪q, preventing escape from I⁻(q) between two level-surface visits. This is exactly the supplied mixed causal/chronological implication.
